title: Influence of short high-intensity training and tea on extracellular inflammasome particles - pilot study
summary:
During physical exertion, certain particles can be released into the bloodstream, which can trigger inflammation in the body. Particularly intense physical activity leads to an increase in these particles. Tea, especially tea made from elecampane root, is said to have anti-inflammatory properties that may influence this reaction.

Research question:
The study investigates whether short, intense physical exertion leads to an increase in these pro-inflammatory particles in the blood and whether drinking elecampane root tea before exertion can reduce this increase.

Methodology:
Healthy participants perform a short, intense exercise session on two different days, consisting of squats, push-ups, and jumps until exhaustion. On one day, they drink elecampane root tea before exercise, and on the other day, they drink the same amount of water. Blood samples are taken before, immediately after, and approximately 24 hours after exercise to measure the concentration of the particles. The order of the days is determined randomly, and there is a break of at least 72 hours between exercises.

none
Exclusion criteria:
• Contraindication against maximum exertion according to the recommendation of the German Society of Cardiology (H.-J. Trappe and H. Löllgen)
• Lack of consent
• Pregnancy
